data.hypothesis: A warp-shuffle reduction followed by one shared exchange of four warp partials should reduce CTA-wide synchronization from the baseline tree’s repeated barriers to one per block. The recursive 128-element pass geometry stays fixed; 64-bit partials prevent overflow in intermediate groups when the valid final sum fits int. Added wide arithmetic and scratch traffic could offset the synchronization savings, so no whole-call speedup is assumed.
data.notes: The supplied baseline is valid on 10 cases across five sizes and two seeds; its three full-call samples average 46.4832 microseconds. This candidate has not been validated or measured here. The compact ping-pong buffers use caller scratch without allocation, retain the recursive pass count and final asynchronous device-to-device copy, and are bounded by the baseline’s larger scratch regions for sizes requiring multiple passes. Request all required correctness cases and repeated full-call measurements before drawing a performance conclusion. The consulted CUDA guide snapshot is publisher-current and does not establish the frozen target/compiler version; the baseline already uses the synchronized warp-shuffle intrinsic.
transformations: Replace the modulo/shared-memory reduction tree with warp shuffles, four shared warp partials, and one CTA barrier; retain 128 threads and one input per lane.
Accumulate recursive partials in signed 64-bit values and narrow only when the final reduction writes the int result.
Retain the recursive ceil(count/128) passes, caller-supplied scratch, default-stream launches, and final asynchronous device-to-device copy.
